origin: Adapts an identifiable published use-case idea, prompt, or workflow whose license permits reuse. The original creator, the license, and the exact changes are all recorded.

Written for this collection by adapting identifiable openly licensed sources, such as a published use-case idea, a guide that documents an AI operation, or a source item, and joining them with ideas from open-access books on teaching. Each source, its license, and what was taken from it are recorded.
Written for this collection without adapting any source’s wording or structure. The works whose ideas shape the design are cited, so its reasoning can be traced.

aside.gist: A syllabus AI policy governs what students may do. These use-case ideas are the instructor’s, or a colleague’s, or the library’s.
aside.label: The instructor’s own work
aside.reads: Not governed by a course AI policy. Institutional policy on staff use, and any disclosure your discipline expects of authors, still apply.
aside.rule: the actor is not a student

local.label: Syllabi Policies on the Gen AI Faculty & Staff Guide

policy.note: Every use-case idea in the collection carries the position it assumes. That is derived from the record — from whether the model touches submitted work, whether the work is assessed, and what disclosure the design asks for — not from anyone’s view about what a course policy ought to say. A use-case idea sitting at one position is not a recommendation to adopt that position.

source.name: Classroom Policies for AI Generative Tools
source.note: The worked examples below were drawn from this open, crowdsourced collection of course AI policies, which is added to continuously. Each quotation keeps the instructor, the course, the institution, and the license the contributor placed it under. The four positions are a reading of that collection, not a scheme anyone has to adopt.

tiers.gist: AI is welcome for studying and skill-building, but never for the work you submit.

items.quote: You are expected to use the university's AI tutor each week as a study coach … [but] do not use any AI to generate answers for homework, worksheets, or projects. Copying or paraphrasing AI output is prohibited.

Don't. Unless you receive explicit instructor permission, do not submit materials produced by … 'generative AI' in this course. You also may not use them for research or summarization of course materials.

No AI use for writing assignments … is permitted … Using tools for spellcheck and grammar is perfectly fine — and recommended. [This] class is carefully designed to help you learn the subject, think critically, and write thoughtfully.
All assignments should be prepared by the student… AI-generated submissions are not permitted and will be treated as plagiarism.
Please do not use Generative AI tools as a substitute for your own thinking, reflections, and voice… None of you are mediocre, and you deserve better.

tiers.label: Practice, not products
tiers.reads: Runs in a course where nothing the model touched may be handed in.
tiers.rule: the model is held back from the submitted work, or nothing graded comes out of it

tiers.gist: Generative AI is off-limits unless an instructor explicitly allows it — often case by case.

items.quote: Students … are not permitted to utilize Generative AI at any stage … unless explicitly noted in the instructions for a deliverable. Students may formally request, in writing, an exception … considered on a case-by-case basis.

Students are allowed to employ generative A.I. tools in specific exercises when instructed so … If an A.I. tool is actually used, an addendum must be turned in with each exercise, with a live link to the chat for accountability.

items.course: Sample statement: “use only with prior permission”
items.quote: Students are allowed to use … (artificial intelligence … such as ChatGPT or Dall-E) on assignments … if instructor permission is obtained in advance. Unless given permission …, each student is expected to complete each assignment without … automated tools.
Use of generative AI tools only with prior permission… you must highlight information retrieved using generative AI and cite it properly.
In general, you may not use AI to complete homework or group work assignments. If you are permitted to use it for a specific assignment, I will say so.

tiers.label: By permission only
tiers.reads: Needs the instructor to have said, for this assignment, that the tool is allowed.
tiers.rule: the model enters assessed work under the instructor’s own authorization

tiers.gist: Use is optional — but if you use it, trace it, cite it, and own the output.

items.quote: You will never be required to use AI … Work created with generative AI will likely lead to a lower grade … If you use AI, you must trace its claims to sources, cite them, and remain accountable for the information.

AI is a tool, not a shortcut! … You are accountable for all work with your name on it … For every assignment, students shall include an AI disclosure statement specifying which tools were used, how they contributed, and the portions they influenced.

The key goal of our course … is to use words, sources, and technology tools in transparent, accountable, and ethical ways … If you decide to use a Generative AI tool … reflect that use in your submitted work.
The burden does not fall on the instructor to prove that AI was used, but rather on the student to prove that learning has occurred.
When using AI to research topics, you must cite any information obtained from AI sources, just as you would with books, articles, or websites.
AI is a tool, but one that you need to acknowledge using… Using these tools without proper citation constitutes plagiarism.

tiers.label: Disclose & be accountable
tiers.reads: Comes with its own disclosure: the design already asks for a log, a trace, or a statement.
tiers.rule: the use-case idea itself requires the use to be recorded

tiers.gist: AI use is encouraged when it supports learning — just cite how you used it.

items.quote: You are welcome to use AI tools … unless otherwise specified. However, you must cite it as a source, including a description of how you used it … Thoughtful use is encouraged; use that replaces learning is frowned upon.

I encourage you to use AI-related technologies in this class … For research, AI use is encouraged … For coding, you are welcome to treat AI as a tutor … For written content, please write a draft … before using AI to help improve it.

This course encourages the … ethical/responsible use of AI/ML, Generative AI, and Agentic tools … What I ask in return is (1) transparency in use, and (2) willingness to share … prompts, code, and other artifacts.
AI writing tools can be helpful resources for thinking as well as writing. I encourage students to use them to think through questions throughout the course.
You are encouraged to explore the use of generative AI tools to improve learning… you are responsible for ensuring the accuracy, ethics, and proper citation of any information generated.

tiers.label: Welcomed, with citation
tiers.reads: Assumes use is fine and asks the student to say how the tool was used.
tiers.rule: the use-case idea asks only for an acknowledgment
